Messages.Author: X_Zealot
Messages.Body:
> "...Superior Sanguinous: As above, but with two additional strikes each
round."
>
> I had (basic) Latin in school but the suffix -ous we never covered. :-)
>
> Jeroen

I believe it is greek which was then blended into Latin actually.
I belive it means "of, or relating to".
Webster lists it as "full of : abounding in : having : possessing the
qualities of "

Good examples are

Androgynous is having the characteristics or nature of both male and female
Andro meaning man
Gyn meaning woman

Polymorphous is having, assuming, or occurring in various forms, characters,
or styles
Poly meaning many
morph meaning form

So Sanguinous would be
Sanguin meaning blood
-ous meaning "of, or refering to"
therefore it would me "of or refering to blood" which is how Sanguinous
works. All the Blood Brothers share the same blood.

Comments Welcome,
Norman S. Brown, Jr.
XZealot
